cohort: The study included 880,182 live births recorded in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, between 2012 and 2021.
finding: Healthcare and socioeconomic factors, particularly the type of hospital, were more predictive of cesarean section rates than obstetric factors, and the overall chance of a cesarean section decreased by 26% in 2021 compared to 2012.
mod_finding: The chance of having a cesarean section was 26% lower in 2021 compared to the series's first year, likely due to primary care and comprehensive obstetric care policies.
